title: Audit and fix rate-limit credit matching for asynchronous webhook arrivals and timezone boundary skew
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported invoice mismatches where rate-limit credit lines were either missing or split across adjacent hourly invoice lines. The pattern correlates with webhook arrival after the hourly aggregation window during daylight saving time (DST) transitions and high retry backpressure. Root cause hypothesis: asynchronous webhook processing and webhook retry/backfill pipeline emit credit events with local-time rounding applied by a conversion helper; downstream hourly aggregator normalizes timestamps to UTC but has an off-by-one-hour rounding edge-case around DST transitions. Additional contributing factors: webhook ingestion queue reordering during retries, a non-idempotent credit dedup key that uses local-hour + customer_id (instead of absolute event_id), and the Netsuite export mapper assuming UTC-bucketed invoice lines.

Impact: customers experience duplicate or missing small-credit invoice lines (typically < $1 each) that aggregate to material differences for high-volume accounts. This causes support tickets and manual adjustments in Netsuite reconciliations. Because credits are applied as negative invoice lines, duplicates can cause over-crediting and revenue recognition headaches.

Goals: 1) Fix production pipeline to ensure all rate-limit credit events are attributed deterministically to the correct billing hour (UTC). 2) Add detection/alerting for skewed credit distributions. 3) Backfill and reconcile historical misattributed credits for the last 90 days where material. 4) Harden export process to emit idempotent Netsuite lines and preserve original event_ids for audit.

Investigation notes and technical findings:
- Aggregator uses SQL rollup on credits table with GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', local_ts) which was introduced as optimization during onboarding of a regional local-time display feature; this is the primary cause for local-to-UTC misbuckets.
- The webhook ingestion library (ingest-credit-service) applies a helper that does toLocalHour(event_ts, customer_tz) before storing credit_bucket, to support a UX report. That helper does not use timezone-aware DST-safe conversions in a small edge-case when tz database shifts.
- Dedup key computed in credits_emitter: CONCAT(customer_id, '|', customer_local_hour, '|', credit_amount). This is not durable for retries across DST boundary or when the same event is retried in a different process with slightly different local_hour rounding.
- A race exists: delayed webhook processed after aggregation window but before export snapshot causes export to see both previously exported aggregated credit and a late-arriving credit, leading to split lines on export. Export dedup in export-mapper is based on composite (customer_id, export_hour) — mismatch between credit dedup key and export dedup key.

Proposed changes (implementation plan):
1) Short term (patch, low-risk, 48h):
   - Remove storing local-hour on the canonical credits table. Persist raw_event_timestamp (UTC) and customer_tz separately. Compute display-time in reporting paths only.
   - Change dedup key to use immutable event_id (provided by gateway) when available, fallback to sha256(event_payload) for older webhook producers.
   - Tighten aggregator SQL to GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', event_ts_utc) consistently.
   - Add a guard in export-mapper to canonicalize timestamps to UTC before bucketing and to include original_event_id in the Netsuite line memo field for audit.
2) Medium term (backfill & verification, 2 weeks):
   - Write backfill script that finds credits where export_bucket != date_trunc('hour', event_ts_utc) AND abs(timestamp_diff_in_seconds) > 300. Mark candidates and compute corrective adjustment lines (net negative/positive) grouped by invoice and customer.
   - Run reconciliation dry-run against staging: compare totals per-customer per-billing-day between current exports and corrected exports; produce a reconciler report.
   - For confirmed material differences (> $5/day/customer), schedule manual Netsuite adjustments with Finance and surface a patch export to import corrections via the Netsuite CSV import flow.
3) Long term (prevention, ongoing):
   - Add an end-to-end test in CI that simulates DST boundary webhooks with retries and validates aggregator/idempotency.
   - Add Prometheus metric and alert: percent_of_credit_events_where(abs(bucket_offset_seconds) > 3600) > 0.01% over 1h.
   - Update runbook with steps to examine event timelines and run the backfill.

Backfill algorithm sketch (pseudocode):
- SELECT event_id, customer_id, event_ts_utc, export_hour, exported_amount FROM credit_exports WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '90 days';
- For each row: correct_bucket = date_trunc('hour', event_ts_utc); if correct_bucket != export_hour then accumulate delta[customer_id][invoice_day] += exported_amount (sign depends on whether exported line needs reassigning or reversing);
- Emit corrective records: for each (customer, invoice_day) where abs(delta) > backfill_threshold, create a backfill_plan record with reason=\"timezone-bucket-skew\" and commands to create reversing invoice and correct invoice. Attach original_event_ids for audit.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for new dedup key logic (event_id fallback) and canonical UTC bucketing.
- Integration tests: run ingest-credit-service locally with injected clocks (simulate DST forward/back) and verify aggregator output unchanged for non-edge windows and corrected for edge windows.
- Staging export run with synthetic events (10k events) to ensure no regression in volume and no duplicate dedup collisions.

Rollout plan:
- Deploy ingest-credit-service patch to a small shard (shard-7) with traffic split 5% initial.
- Monitor error rate, credit aggregation differentials, and export deltas for 6 hours. Promote progressively to 50%/100% if green.
- Once production aggregator and export pipeline are stable, run backfill dry-run, circulate findings to Finance, and schedule correction import in a low-traffic maintenance window.

Monitoring and detection:
- New adhoc query for support dashboard: SELECT customer_id, billing_day, count(*) AS credit_lines, sum(credit_amount) FROM exported_credits WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '14 days' GROUP BY customer_id, billing_day ORDER BY sum(credit_amount) DESC LIMIT 100;
- Add Grafana panel: \"Credit lines per invoice (90d)\" with alert when a single invoice has > 200 credit lines or > 0.5% of invoices have > 50 credit lines (indicative of duplicates).

Manual remediation steps for support:
1) Run support tool 'credit-audit' for customer to list all exported_event_ids and timestamps.
2) If duplicates are minimal, file a manual Netsuite adjustment with Finance attaching the audit csv. If duplicates are widespread, escalate to oncall for backfill plan.

Open questions / blockers:
- Need Finance/Netsuite team access to perform CSV correction imports. (Owner: Marisol Ramos)
- Confirm whether gateway always provides immutable event_id for older webhook producers. If not, we need to enable sha256 fallback and accept imperfect matching for historical events.
- Estimate of affected customers in last 90 days — need historical aggregation job run to compute. (blocked by access to large export snapshot; request queued with infra)

References / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleDesignDoc (internal) 
- PR (ingest dedup and UTC bucket): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-credit-service/pull/1342
- Backfill prototype (not merged): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-backfills/pull/88
- Support dashboard query gist: https://gist.github.com/gabeliu/credit-audit-query

Estimated rollback risk: low for dedup-change if we restrict to event_id-first logic; medium for backfill (requires manual finance coordination).
